questions.question_description: Implement a Binary Search Tree (BST). Read N integers to construct the BST. Print the Preorder traversal of the resulting BST.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers for insertion.
questions.output_format: A single line containing space-separated integers for the Preorder traversal. Print 'Empty' if the tree is empty (N=0).
questions.hints: For Preorder traversal, process the root node first, then recursively traverse the left subtree, followed by the right subtree.
questions.solution_explanation: A Node structure is defined, elements are inserted and then Preorder traversal is applied which visits root, left subtree, then right subtree.

questions.question_description: Implement a Binary Search Tree (BST). Read N integers to construct the BST. Print the Inorder traversal of the resulting BST.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers for insertion.
questions.output_format: A single line containing space-separated integers for the Inorder traversal. Print 'Empty' if the tree is empty (N=0).
questions.hints: Inorder traversal of a BST always yields elements in sorted order. Recursively traverse the left subtree, then process root node, then right subtree.
questions.solution_explanation: Elements are inserted comparing values and the Inorder traversal is applied visiting left subtree, root, right subtree respectively.

questions.question_description: Implement a Binary Search Tree (BST). Read N integers to construct the BST. Print the Postorder traversal of the resulting BST.
questions.input_format: Integer N, followed by N space-separated integers for insertion.
questions.output_format: A single line containing space-separated integers for the Postorder traversal. Print 'Empty' if the tree is empty (N=0).
questions.hints: For Postorder traversal, recursively traverse the left subtree, then the right subtree, and finally process the root node.
questions.solution_explanation: Elements are inserted comparing values and the Postorder traversal visits left subtree, right subtree then root.
